[serious][dramatic] Jesus told his hometown one old story — and they tried to throw him off a cliff. This is the story.

[matter-of-fact] Naaman: a great general — and a leper. A servant girl pointed him to a prophet. Elisha didn't even come out. He sent one line: wash in the Jordan, seven times.

[serious] Naaman was furious:

[rapid-fire][emphasized] <speaker name="naaman">"Are not Abana and Pharpar, rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel? may I not wash in them, and be clean?"</speaker>

[quietly] His own servants stopped him:

[reflective][slow] <speaker name="servants">"My father, if the prophet had bid thee do some great thing, wouldest thou not have done it? how much rather then, when he saith to thee, Wash, and be clean?"</speaker>

[awe][slow] He went down. He washed, seven times. New skin, like a child's.

[serious][deliberate] This is the story Jesus told — centuries later, to his own hometown:

[deliberate][emphasized] <speaker name="jesus">"Many lepers were in Israel in the time of Eliseus the prophet; and none of them was cleansed, saving Naaman the Syrian."</speaker>

[reflective][deliberate] The best thing Naaman ever did was lose an argument. If the cure feels beneath you — too plain, too easy, too small — that's the same argument. It's still worth losing.
